about: One channel's messages in Slack's own documented conversations.history shape, written down once here so the tests exercise the shapes Slack actually returns rather than the shape a parser happens to want. `at` is an offset in seconds from the moment the watch was turned on and `slack.ts` turns it into a `ts`: a fixture with a fixed epoch in it is a test that passes until some date and then fails for a reason nobody can read. `ME` in text stands for the app's own user id, which `slack.ts` fills in, because a mention is `<@U…>` and the id is only known at run time. `threads` holds each thread WHOLE — the root first, then every reply, including one that was also sent to the channel and so appears in `messages` as well — because that is exactly the difference between what conversations.replies answers and what conversations.history can see.

messages.about: Somebody asking the app for something. The ordinary case, and the one that costs no second request.
messages.text: <@ME> the export button 500s when nothing is selected

messages.about: A message in the channel that is not addressed to the app. Not a request: the mention is the trigger, so a channel need not be a dedicated one.

messages.about: An ask that was edited. `ts` does not move and `edited.ts` does, which is why the revision is the edit.

messages.about: An ask with a thread under it. `reply_count` is what says a second request is needed at all.
messages.text: <@ME> login is slow for everybody this morning

messages.about: A mention inside a thread that somebody also sent to the channel. The only kind of in-thread mention a poll can see at all.
A mention inside a thread that was NOT also sent to the channel. conversations.history does not return these, so this one is here only to prove the selector refuses it if it ever arrives.
A channel event. Not somebody asking for anything, and the allowlist of subtypes is what keeps it out.
An app posting to the channel, mentioning Tade. A subtype the allowlist does not have, so it is not a candidate at all.
An app posting as a user: bot_id and no subtype, so it reaches the rule and is refused there as is_bot.

messages.about: A file somebody dropped with an ask about it. The files are references and nothing is downloaded.
An ask Slack names nobody for. There is no authorisation question to ask about it, so it selects nothing.
